summary.name: Snipaste
summary.one_liner: Snipaste is a screenshot tool that captures screen regions and pins them back onto the screen as topmost floating image windows.
use_cases: capture a screen region and keep it visible on top while working
compare reference images beside other windows
annotate screenshots with shapes, text, and blur
pick colors from anywhere on screen
paste clipboard images or text as floating windows
summary.what_it_does: Snipaste captures a screen region with a hotkey (F1 by default, per the page) and lets you paste the capture as a floating window with F3. Floating windows can be zoomed, rotated, flipped, made translucent, and set to mouse click-through. It can also turn clipboard content (images, plain text, HTML, color info, or image files such as PNG, JPG, GIF, and TIFF) into a floating window. The snipping mode includes auto-detection of UI elements, pixel-level control, a color picker, and history playback. Annotation tools include rectangle, ellipse, line strip, arrow, pencil, marker, text, mosaic, Gaussian blur, eraser, and undo/redo.
notable: Pins screenshots as topmost floating windows that can be zoomed, rotated, made translucent, or click-through
Converts clipboard text and color info into floating image windows
Pixel-level snipping with auto UI element detection and a built-in color picker
Customizable hotkeys, theme, and interface font
